schemes.label: Capacity Market
schemes.attribution_note: Only the part of the Capacity Market that net zero caused is counted. Any power system needs backup, so each year's levy is reduced by what the same system without net-zero policy would have paid at that year's capacity price for its own backup; the remainder is counted. Shares for 2016-2025 come from a model of that system; later years use the 2025 share (14.6%) until the model covers them. The figure is a floor: a 550 g/kWh emissions limit has kept about 11 GW of coal out of the four-year-ahead auctions since 2021, and capacity prices rose after it; no published source measures how much of that rise net zero caused, so none of it is counted.

extras.source: LCCC data portal, capacity market payments

schemes.label: Climate Change Levy (electricity share)
schemes.attribution_note: Electricity's share of CCL main-rate liabilities (HMRC's published commodity split of declarations). Gas/solid-fuel main-rate CCL is excluded. Carbon Price Support is counted in the carbon line.

extras.source: HMRC Environmental Taxes Bulletin (formerly Climate Change Levy and Carbon Price Floor Bulletin), March 2026 edition, tables ODS (2026_March_env_tabs_test.ods), Table 1b "CCL and CPF receipts and clearances data by calendar year": electricity main-rate declared liabilities (the only commodity split HMRC publishes), rounded down to the nearest GBP 0.1m, as read by the shared cost register (line CCL_ELEC). Carbon Price Support is not in this line: it is part of the carbon line's tax collected (aios-harness#44).

schemes.label: Carbon in the electricity price
schemes.attribution_note: The whole carbon effect on the electricity price: each year's carbon cost in the wholesale price of power in Great Britain, as the gas-counterfactual engine models it. Part of it is tax collected by the Treasury (Carbon Price Support and the power sector's share of UK emissions-trading auction receipts); the rest is carbon in the price that no one collected as tax.

schemes.label: Constraint turn-up (paid to switch on)
schemes.attribution_note: Estimated cost of paying other stations to replace the wind energy switched off for network constraints: each half-hour's switched-off wind volume priced against that half-hour's accepted offers (Octopus Energy Wasted Wind method). Taken out of the balancing (BSUoS) uplift, never more than it, so no total changes.

extras.source: Elexon Insights settlement stacks (bids and offers)

schemes.label: Balancing costs (BSUoS uplift)
schemes.attribution_note: Raw totals stored; attribution happens in the money model. Only each year's cost above what the same year would have cost without net-zero policy (the gas-counterfactual engine's balancing road, GO4, reference/model_pin.yaml) is attributed, NET of wind constraint payments already counted in the direct layer; a year below it counts as negative (signed years, as Reliable Britain). The estimated cost of replacing switched-off wind (constraint turn-up) is then shown as its own line and taken out of this one.
